overview: This Senate resolution marks the 150th anniversary of the Battle of the Little Bighorn, fought June 25 and 26, 1876, in southeastern Montana, and known to many tribes as the Battle of Greasy Grass. It recounts the background, including the 1868 Treaty of Fort Laramie and the conflict that followed after gold was found in the Black Hills, and describes how Lakota Sioux, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho forces led by Sitting Bull, Crazy Horse and others defeated Lieutenant Colonel George Custer's 7th Cavalry. It notes the battle's lasting importance to the tribal nations whose ancestors fought there. The resolution honors all the soldiers, scouts, civilians and warriors who died and encourages people to visit the Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument. It does not change any law or spending. As of June 24, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say it recognizes a pivotal event in American and tribal history and honors those on all sides who died.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law, treaty obligation or spending.
